one_star_reviews.text:
Very disapointing experience with DM Keith Skoda Hull today - having called on Tuesday to arrange the purchase of a used Skoda Kamiq that we saw online we managed to get a deposit down on the car the next day after a little back and fourth on the phone.

They were relitively helpful on the phone and sent a video which was about as streamlined as the service got, the video flagged some bodywork defects and they promised that they could fix them. We decided, great, we could strike a deal if this was resolved for pick up this Friday -understanding that this was a tight turn around, we mentioned at the time if it could be done then that is OK, if not we would look elsewhere as we were based in Scotland. They assured us it would be fine and it would be ready to pick up by 3.30pm on Friday afternoon.

On Wednesday they sent the paperwork, and after reviewing this there was numerous discrepancies in the listed details, firstly, the milage was listed wrong, it had done 1000 more miles than it said on the paperwork (which would have voided the 30 day warranty had we not spotted it) and the amount of GAP insurance we decided to opt into was listed as 8k-12k for a 13.5k car - we pointed this out and there was a slow and uninterested response on the phone.

Having chased them numerous times on Wednesday and Thursday about the afformentioned issue, and given Jack, Shaun and the team numerous opportunites correct these discrepancies my patience was wearing a little thin but when I finally got through just around lunchtime Thursday I was assured it would be all fine and that the paper work would be ready. At that point I had assumed that everything was tickity boo with the repair works we had been promised as no one mentioned it. Give them a chance I said to myself, car salespeople must be finding it hard at the moment.

Last minuite on Thursday, I get the next day off work to come and collect the car.

We then get to 11am today (Friday)  having driven half way across the country to pick up the car - and 3 hours into my journey they phoned to say it would not be ready for collection as none of the work had been completed (why not call me when they opened at 8am?! or even mention there had been no progress the day before?)

They, to their credit did offer a sort of half baked solution after an hour or two - of which I spent at in a service station waiting - its now 1PM. 2 hours away from Hull. Their solution was that they would get the bodywork done elsewhere, i.e. that they could get a bodyshop in Edinburgh to repair it - when I asked who it was they could not give me a name. They offered £200 off for the numerous issues raised for a £13,500 car which we were paying in cash up front for.

After driving a bit towards Hull, I pulled off in a layby on the York junction in a car that I have been wanting to trade in for some time, after me and my partner saving up for an extremely long time and making so many sacrifices to buy oursleves a new car. Bubbling up in me there was nothing I could do but feel anything but a sense of helplessness and anger at the situation. Why did they not tell me sooner? Why was it me chasing them through the whole process? Why did they seem so nonchalant about the situation when they new that I was driving from Scotland that very day? Why, when a customer is paying a third of an average UK salary for a second hand product are people just not bothered at all?

Now on my way back to Edinburgh after around 7 hours of constant driving I am writing this again in another service station. The 'trust' in the fact that when you buy a car, you are not being just being completely fleeced has well and truely eroded - I used to think that official dealerships were meant to be trustworthy and that Skoda, the brand, was all about reliablility this experience has done nothing but prove to me the antithisis of this sentiment.

Safe to say I will be taking my custom and our hard earned money elsewhere. To be honest, it has pretty much put me off buying a Skoda all together, thank you DM Keith Skoda Hull for your service.

Shaun is as absolutely amazing and met all our needs, top service I couldn’t recommend more.

My business had high expectations after a very positive initial meeting, but unfortunately the service that followed was deeply disappointing.

After being handed over to operations, communication was extremely poor from the outset. I had to chase to find out when work was starting, I never had a clear sense of what was being done or why, and when I raised concerns, it became clear that assumptions had been made instead of there being any kind of proper strategy discussion. Reporting was also weak, with little explanation provided, and at one point I was even sent an SEO report for another business.

What stood out most was the complete lack of care and attention. I did not feel valued as a client, and I did not feel there was any proper care taken in how my account was managed.

When I later raised these concerns, the response was effectively that I was on the Bronze package. In my view, regardless of package level, if a client is paying for a service, there should still be a proper standard of care, attention, communication and professionalism at all times throughout the contract lifecycle.

My final issue is that, despite the investment made over the contract period, I have finished this engagement with no clear understanding of what impact the work actually had or what value it delivered, if any at all. That should never be the case with a professional SEO service.

To their credit, they did acknowledge some of the communication and process issues when I complained. However, I was disappointed with how the matter was ultimately handled. Sometimes when a service falls short, the way a company responds can help restore confidence, but I did not feel that happened here.

This review is simply an honest reflection of my experience. Based on that experience, I would not use this company again or recommend them to others.

A real shame.

The Court has great historic value and the characterful building previously was, (and still has the potential to be), an excellent place to live, but the experience is now overshadowed by the hassle of dealing with the ineffective John Lewis management team, who took ownership of the building in Oct/Nov 2023, and the building appears to suffer from poor maintenance as it is in noticeably deteriorating condition compared to when I moved in in March 2023.

The building, though historic, does not appear to be maintained to a good standard and parts of the building appear to be deteriorating quite quickly, as pictured. The front gates of the development are also regularly broken (unlocked) and the main lift is often out of use. Due to recent bad weather, the roof of the Court has also leaked in certain areas of the building, rendering stairwells out of use.

I often saw fly-tipping in the surrounding area in which the development is situated (see picture) and smash-and-grabs from parked cars on the main road in the summers were a real problem. The local shop is also, from what the staff say, constantly dealing with armed robberies.

The management team, although friendly in person, are extremely hard to get in contact with and provide unreasonably slow responses to emails, sometimes upwards of eleven days, despite repeated chaser telephone calls and emails. It should not be that hard for a tenant to receive a response to an email within a reasonable time-frame (and was not so with the previous management). Though I was prepared to give them the benefit of the doubt on the first few occasions that emails went unanswered or had unreasonable delays in response, this unprofessional level of communication unfortunately was commonplace and regretfully became expected. Upon visiting the reception office in person in attempts to seek clarity or resolve issues, I was, on numerous occasions, told that what I had said/requested would be 'passed on' to the manager or, on some occasions, would be actioned but yet it often transpired that messages were not passed on & action was not taken or, when it was, it was only so after further chasing. Clear and effective communication from the new John Lewis management is lacking and this view appears to be the consensus amongst the majority of residents. The housekeeping staff and the security team are worthy of praise and are friendly, and though other tenants voiced to me that they sometimes found certain security guards a little abrasive when asked whether a parcel has arrived, this was not my experience.

In my second year of living there I moved to a new room and the battery in my front door fob, which was necessary to access my apartment, died on approximately five occasions, over the course of a few months from May 24, on these repeated occasions rendering me locked out of the room and so I had to go to the reception and on all but one of these occasions I was assisted by Joe, one of the members of staff, who was able to change the internal door battery, and was always helpful and apologetic. However the third occasion in which the fob broke took place on a weekend in late June 24 (when the management staff are not on site) and, due to the door handle also not being fully operational (and thus the lock un-openable by the guard's site master key), I was locked out for 4.5 hours and had to await a locksmith's arrival from Dewsbury in order to gain access to the room; it was very disappointing that I was locked out of my own room, given that the situation would've not been unforeseen/could've been avoided by management in that 1. I had been told on the second occasion that I was locked out that a replacement door monitor would be ordered to ensure that I was not locked out again but yet the monitor was not replaced and 2. I had raised the faulty door handle on two occasions – on my check in report upon initial move-in into the new room in April 24 and also on the first occasion in which my door fob died in early May 24 but yet the handle was not repaired.

Avoid.

88% one star ratings on Trust Pilot! Do you actually care about your customers?

​I am writing this to warn prospective buyers: Do not be fooled by the "premium" branding of the Husqvarna Automower 450x. While the hardware is marketed as a high-end, long-term investment, my experience has proven that Husqvarna has no interest in supporting its customers once they have your money. Into my 4th Season with a fault every season since new, purchased 2022.

Within one month, a new transformer, then new charging cable and contacts finally new communication board. All within the space of three years. The mower always in garage when parked.
​1. Planned Obsolescence via "3G Sunset"
​I spent thousands on a flagship 450x, a machine sold on the promise of "Smart" connectivity. Now, because of the 3G network shutdown—a transition that was well-known in the industry for years—the "smart" features of my mower are dead. Husqvarna’s response? They expect the customer to foot the bill for a 4G upgrade kit just to regain the functionality I already paid for at retail. For a premium brand, selling a product with a "built-in expiration date" on its core features is deceptive and unprofessional.
​2. Software Logic that Defeats the Purpose
​The mower’s programming is infuriatingly "too smart for its own good." Despite setting a 12-hour mowing window, the mower frequently decides the grass "doesn't need cutting" due to the erratic Weather Timer and stays in the dock. It will sit at 100% charge, displaying "Mowing according to schedule," while the lawn grows wild. You end up spending more time babysitting the app and the keypad than you would have spent just pushing a manual mower.
​3. Customer Service: The "Goodwill" Trap
​When you reach out for help, Husqvarna’s customer service is a masterclass in deflection. Their latest response to me was that because they had performed a "goodwill" repair on a faulty charging station in the past, they are now refusing to help with the connectivity failure. They view basic product support as a "favour" they can use against you later. Once your warranty is up, you are on your own, regardless of whether the failure is due to their poor technical planning.
​4. Conclusion: Look Elsewhere
​The robotic mower market is no longer a monopoly. There are now numerous competitors (Mammotion, Worx, Segway) offering better tech, better connectivity (RTK/Wi-Fi), and arguably better support for a fraction of the price.
​Husqvarna is resting on a reputation they no longer deserve. If you want a mower that actually mows when you tell it to, and a company that stands behind its "flagship" products, do not buy a Husqvarna.

I commissioned NES&E for a standard domestic beam design. I'm an Incorporated Electrical Engineer myself so appreciate professional standards.

Their engineer attended my property, took measurements, yet issued a drawing that simply does not reflect reality. Multiple structural elements were shown which do not exist in their stated location — an error visible from the very room they took the measurements from.

When I challenged it, they amended part of the drawing but offered no apology for the lazy attempt at accuracy, instead, being rude. When I phoned to discuss it, I was told "this is as basic as it gets".

Since it is as basic as it gets, a Chartered Structural Engineer should not issue drawings that contradict the physical building they've "inspected". A Chartered Structural Engineer should know the difference between a supporting wall and a stud wall, and not attempt a calculation based on an structure which is simply not there.

Also, a professional firm should apologise when caught making such basic mistakes. NES&E did not. Therefore, I cannot recommend them.

If they make such obvious mistakes on basic jobs, what will they do with complex arrangements? I would not trust them professionally.

Edit:
Rather than admit they made mistakes, they instead opt to double-down and make irrelevant and childish points against their own client - see their reply to this review.

You don't have to be a structural engineer to know that a drawing does not match what is physically in front of you, and you especially don't have to be a structural engineer to know professionalism. My original review stands, and their reply only reinforces it.

⭐ 1-Star Review: Extremely Disappointing Spa Day – Would Not Return
I visited Burntwood Court for a spa day with my mum last Friday and unfortunately we left hugely disappointed. For £200, we expected a relaxing, pampering experience, but the facilities and the way our concerns were handled fell well short.

Facilities & Cleanliness
The spa is extremely dated and feels more like a basic leisure centre than a spa offering a “luxury” experience. There was an issue with the boiler which meant the main pool was absolutely freezing—so much so that regular gym members were walking out of the aqua aerobics class. The hydrotherapy pool was barely tepid and, more concerning, the water was so cloudy and dirty that you couldn’t see the bottom. Several regulars told us that the pool temperatures have been inconsistent for weeks.

Customer Service & Handling of Complaints
After less than an hour, we spoke to the lady on reception to explain how disappointed we were. She and a gentleman behind the desk were very understanding and initially told us a refund could be arranged. As we were getting changed to leave, we were then told that the spa manager (Kat Backhouse), who wasn’t even on site, had refused the refund because “the water temperatures were within a couple of degrees of accepted levels.” No acknowledgement was given regarding the filthy water.

I asked to speak to the manager, only to be told she wasn’t in and that she would speak to me before my treatment. She never came to find me. Instead, we were offered the option of moving our lunch and treatments earlier so we could leave sooner—something we felt we had to accept to avoid losing our money entirely.

Treatments & Food
To give credit where it’s due, the food was decent and the massages themselves were excellent. However, the constant banging from the gym next door to the treatment room completely disrupted what should have been a relaxing experience.

Inconsistency in Compensation
As we were leaving, we spoke to another mother–daughter pair who said they appreciated us raising concerns, as they were also leaving early and had been given complimentary passes. We requested the same but were only given them reluctantly and only after asking multiple times and explaining that others had received them.

Overall
The combination of poor facilities, unclean water, refusal to process a reasonable refund request, and inconsistent customer service left us extremely disappointed. Sadly, despite the lovely therapists, we will not be returning.

Avoid Yorkshire Gas and Power at all costs – a disgraceful company.

My partner is a small business owner and his experience with Yorkshire Gas and Power (YGP) has been nothing short of appalling from start to finish.

Like many others, he received a phone call from a broker and, without fully understanding, was placed into a binding three-year contact as a result of the conversation. He only realised this when the contract appeared in his inbox. I immediately contacted YGP on his behalf, only to be told that his consent to the contract had been obtained legally over the phone, that a signature was not required to secure the contact and that, as a small business, there was no cooling off period. Basically, unless he wanted to pay a huge fee, he was trapped for 3 years!

To make matters worse, YGP then deducted an “advanced energy payment” of just under £500 - which was never mentioned by the broker during his conversation - on top of taking initial overly estimated direct debit payments. This lack of transparency is unacceptable and feels deliberately misleading.

Their customer service was abysmal throughout the contract. Queries were ignored, promises were made and then broken, and getting a straight answer was impossible. Nonetheless, throughout the whole three years every he ensured that every invoice was paid on time by direct debit. Not a single payment was missed.

At the end of the contract, YGP failed to return the balance owed from the advanced energy payment (over £350). I chased this for him multiple times over many months and was repeatedly told it would be paid back. It never was. Every time I contacted them there was a different excuse for the refund not being paid – from ‘admin errors’ to ‘system problems’.

My partner was forced to take the matter to the Energy Ombudsman who, after reviewing all of the evidence submitted, ruled entirely in his favour. YGP were ordered to pay back the money they owed, plus compensation and a letter of apology. Following this decision, YGP waited the full length of time to supply a response, filing it with just a couple of hours left before the ombudsmen’s deadline.

He then had to wait a further week for the payment to be made into his bank account. In all, it has taken a year to receive the refund they owed him, even when the regulator states it should be paid within 10 days of the final meter reading / account being produced.

My advice to all business owners: If a broker ever phones you claiming to offer a “deal” with Yorkshire Gas and Power, put the phone down immediately. Do not engage. Do not trust them. Do not agree to anything.

This company has caused unnecessary stress, wasted time and financial loss. I would never recommend them to any business under any circumstances.
AVOID!!!!

Extremely disappointing experience with Lloyd Jaguar Land Rover York.

I purchased a Range Rover for close to £89,000 expecting a premium vehicle and premium customer service. Unfortunately, the experience from collection onwards fell far below expectations.

Issues included:

The most frustrating part was later discovering the vehicle had previous hire/fleet-related history which was never disclosed during the sales process.

Whilst some minor items were acknowledged, management refused to offer any meaningful resolution or reflect the vehicle condition in the pricing.

For a main dealer and a vehicle at this price point, I expected significantly better standards, transparency, and customer service.

I have now escalated the matter formally.

Would not recommend based on my experience.

I’m writing this review to share a very disappointing and stressful experience with Land Rover York after purchasing a Jaguar E-Pace.
We bought the car expecting a reliable vehicle from a reputable dealership, especially given the amount of money we paid. Unfortunately, just a couple of weeks after purchase, the car broke down at one of the worst possible times—when my wife had gone into labour. We were left with no choice but to take a taxi to the maternity ward. The vehicle was recovered, and we were told the issue had been addressed, including work on the DPF filter and EGR valve.
However, this was only the beginning. A couple of months later, the car broke down again and had to be recovered once more. Then, just two weeks after that, we were travelling from Newcastle to Manchester for an important medical appointment when the car broke down yet again. Land Rover Assistance advised my wife—who had only recently given birth—to take a taxi with a newborn baby, a car seat, a pram, and an ISOFIX base. This was clearly unrealistic and unsafe. After a long six-hour delay, we were eventually given a very poor-quality courtesy vehicle from Enterprise, by which point we had already missed our medical appointment.
Following yet another breakdown, Land Rover Assistance identified and documented a fault before sending the vehicle back to Land Rover York for repair. Despite this, the dealership has now refused to carry out the repair, stating that because the engine management light had been reset by Land Rover Assistance, they would not proceed.
We are now left with a car that is unreliable and, in our view, unsafe. This entire experience has caused significant stress at an already challenging time in our lives. We work hard for what we have and trusted that we were buying from a dealership that would stand behind its vehicles. Sadly, that has not been the case.
I would strongly urge others to think carefully before purchasing from Land Rover York based on our experience.

PLEASE READ – I WOULD HATE FOR THIS TO HAPPEN TO ANYBODY ELSE!!

I bought a Range Rover Discovery Sport in November 2024. The car had been fully serviced by Stratstone and had driven like a dream ever since. I had never experienced a single issue with it and have kept up with all maintenance since owning the car.

In February 2026, a light appeared on the dashboard to say the car was due an oil service. I wanted to take it to a garage that specialised in Land Rovers, so I chose 4X4. The car went in for an oil service on 28th February 2026.

Just four weeks later (April 2026), my car started making strange humming/spinning noises. I took it to a different garage, who carried out a full check. They told me I needed a completely new transfer unit, as it had been totally drained and had no oil in it. They assured me they had checked every inch of the car and there were no oil leaks whatsoever. They said the oil had 100% been drained by a person, which caused the transfer unit to fail.

I have since sought a second opinion, and they confirmed the exact same thing — that the transfer unit had been deliberately drained and not refilled.

The car was in perfect working order before I sent it to 4X4. When I contacted them, they told me they hadn’t touched the transfer unit. However, I certainly have not drained the oil myself, and they were the only garage to work on my car just four weeks prior!!!!

This has cost me £5,700 to repair!!!

I urge anybody considering using this garage to proceed with caution, as I would hate for anyone else to end up in this situation!!!

The charges included items such as a location surcharge, vehicle licence fee and a late return fee, despite the car being returned on time and evidence existing to confirm this.

I contacted customer services to ask for an explanation and they were unable to clearly explain or justify the charges. I specifically requested that no money be taken from my card while the dispute was ongoing, however the payment was still processed.

I might be old fashioned but I have this crazy opinion that when you research rentals, the advertised is the amount you actually pay. You don't get double charged once you return the item in the same condition you received it.

I have now formally disputed the transaction with American Express.

It's cost me about an hour of my time to try and get answers and dispute this and their customer service team seem completely incompetent.

I'd definitely avoid.

If you are being assessed for CCI GET A SECOND OPINION.

My Medserena report said that my scans showed no evidence of CCI, which was a surprise as I had very severe symptoms.

I sent my images to a Neurosurgeon in Spain who specialises in CCI and they told me that my scans are consistent with CCI and AAI and that I have brainstem compression. They showed me on my scans how they'd come to this conclusion and its glaringly obvious when its pointed out. They also said (in passing) that the Medserena scans were of poor quality.
The lady that did my Medserena scans was nice, but seemed quite stressed. She didnt tell me to lean my head on the back of the seat so I was holding my head tilted back totally unsupported and it was too painful I had to press the emergency button, so those images were wasted which was heartbreakingas it was so painful. I had to grab my head with my hands and pull it to upright again as I'd lost all strength.
They didn't tell me until after my scan that the results can take up to 10 days. They didn't send the scans to me, only to my GP, even though I'd self referred. Then after asking for the scans after 10 days they just sent me the report, I had to ask again to finally have access to my images.

All the other staff were lovely, the place was clean and seemed professional. The service they provide is essential as I dont know of anywhere else in the UK that does this kind of scan, but I definitely recommend a second opinion for CCI, which is a shame after you've spent all that money.

Absolutely horrendous care - I would strongly recommend going elsewhere if you have the option.

*UPDATE - I am still in hospital 24 days after the procedure and their organisation to rectify their issue has been poor and mismanaged*

*2nd UPDATE* 8 weeks after lumbar puncture I am still left unable to sit up or walk.

I attended for a lumbar puncture and from the moment I arrived, the experience was chaotic and disorganised.

The nursing staff on the fourth floor didn’t seem to have an understanding of what procedure was going on. I was given conflicting advice about whether to fast or drink fluids after them leaving me waiting around for 4 hours. When the nurses eventually turned up before the procedure, three of them arrived at once and were completely unaligned. The atmosphere was incredibly chaotic and stressful - with all of them arguing/ shouting over each other/ at me to not eat or drink (advice which turned out to be incorrect and I believe this contributed to the complications I experienced afterwards and resulted in me being in and out of NHS A&E for the following 5 days).

After hours of chaos before the procedure, and becoming extremely stressed by the poor quality care, it left me seriously questioning whether to go ahead with the procedure and I got dressed to leave. Unfortunately I decided to proceed after speaking with the consultant, who appeared competent.

Throughout my stay, basic standards of care were repeatedly missed.
A pregnancy test was taken and then lost. The nurses repeatedly tried to attempt put cannulas in my hand/arm and then blew my arm up trying to ‘fix’ it (I have had many of these before and know how it should go). No one seemed to know or care when I should be discharged and I ultimately left without anyone checking on me even though, even though I took a turn after the procedure. Despite clearly stating that I am gluten-free, I was given a meal containing gluten. After the procedure, they forgot to turn my IV fluids back on - despite the fact I had been incorrectly told to fast beforehand and needed hydration and was very dehydrated. Even though downstairs were much better than fourth floor, there was little to no communication between them. They also kept getting mixed up on what medication I should be taking.
To top off the bizarre and erratic care - one of the nurses kept offering me a very awkward ‘hug’, completely misreading the situation (I’m not someone who usually minds a hug but this was completely inappropriate and it was clear that I was obviously not comfortable with her doing so).

Although the team performing the procedure seemed more organised, there was still a noticeable lack of coordination and communication.

Unfortunately, my concerns about their lack of professionalism and disorganisation around me ultimately proved justified when I took a turn after my procedure and the upcoming days after and I ended up being admitted to NHS A&E and staying overnight for several days due to complications from the procedure.

Back at The Cleveland Clinic, once I eventually took myself off to leave after the lumbar puncture procedure (as I just got left with no guidance), I got to the front desk where there was no one so I called the ward manager. When she arrived I raised concerns as I was leaving, even the manager I spoke to had no awareness of who I was or what had happened, which says a lot about the level of oversight.

To make matters worse, when I contacted The Cleveland Clinic about being readmitted a couple of days later due to complications with the procedure they had carried out, (after hours of being put on hold/ignored), I was told that because it was a bank holiday, I would need to pay a £20,000 deposit or £4,000 per night until BUPA offices reopened on Tuesday. After the level of care I received, this was completely unacceptable and to be honest, I think I was probably much safer going into the NHS A and E care anyway.

This is, without question, the worst hospital experience I’ve had. I would not recommend this clinic under any circumstances.

I am a regular patient at your Day Case Centre, and unfortunately I have repeatedly experienced significant difficulties with cannulation at your hospital.

Over time, I have realised that this issue seems to occur far more frequently at Cleveland Clinic than at other hospitals where I have received treatment. This has left me concerned that some staff may not be sufficiently experienced or familiar with difficult cannulation protocols and techniques.

Today, I had to cancel an important day test because cannulation was unsuccessful. This caused unnecessary distress, inconvenience, and a complete waste of my time and money.

As a patient who requires regular treatment, this ongoing issue has become extremely frustrating and anxiety-inducing. I hope the hospital takes this feedback seriously and reviews the training and support available for staff.

one_star_reviews.text:
​Physical Assault, Negligent Safeguarding, and Total Lack of Accountability.

​I am warning parents to be extremely cautious with Sunderland Harriers. My experience involving a physical assault on my son revealing a Club Committee that is failing in its duty of care and deliberately obstructing transparency.

​Assault & Victim Penalization: There were some minor issues at the club with my son due to teasing and cheating when playing games but I was later compelled to make a formal complaint after my son was hit in the face and it escalated to bullying.

The Committee and Welfare Officer’s "solution" was to penalize my son by singling him out to be watched, instead of educating or monitoring the bully. A coach even warned me against moving my son up to the next group because it seemed they couldn't guarantee his safety—effectively prioritizing the attacker's presence over my son's development. My son no longer attends as I feel it is not safe.

Disability Discrimination & Personal Attacks: After a SAR request (Subject Access Request) with UK Athletics I acquired Sunderland Harriers "emergency meeting" notes held 100+ days after the assault.

Club Committee members inappropriately questioned and judged my parenting. They suggested my son required constant supervision due to his disability (despite him attending a regular school and being independent), using these biased assumptions to deflect from the club's own failures.

​Inappropriate & Unsafe Coaching: A coach (who the children did not know) was asked to run a session where he made inappropriate comments and left children to walk back to their parents in the dark by themselves. During this session, children were taken to a nearby lake without any parental consent to train without any other members of staff to help.

​Deliberate Obstruction of Truth: The club leadership refused to communicate via email to avoid creating a paper trail. I was forced to submit two formal complaints to UK Athletics and England Athletics and use a Subject Access Request (SAR) just to get the information the club tried to hide. They would not send information such as their anti bullying policy or disability discrimination policy like other clubs have.

​Gross Safety Risks & Public Dishonesty: The club repeatedly sent children to hill training areas with motorbikes and gangs. I do not know if risk assessments were conducted, but they continued sessions despite knowing the dangers—risks openly discussed on their own Facebook page by their own Welfare Officer. They even denied them happening in a previous Google review while talking about it on Facebook.

​Failure of Supervision & DBS Breaches: Coaches have been leaving children supervised by other children. Furthermore, I and other parents were regularly asked by coaches to help supervise children at night when running in the park. I found I shouldn't have been asked or done this without a DBS check which is a safeguarding breach.

​A "Sham" Investigation: The SAR proved from the club "closed" the bullying case without even having my sons, his friend or my own own written statement on file as evidence that formed the bullying complaint. I made a SAR request for all information from the club and they did notsend the written statement. You cannot  investigate a bullying issue and have a "emergency" committee meeting (100+ days after the incident) about the incident without the complaint. The committee made a  welfare judgment without it.

The club misled England and UK Athletics stating 30 pages of email were sent when it was email threads as they hid the original date they stated they were going to investigate.

​Conclusion:
The Club Committee hides behind phrases like "volunteers run the club" and "DBS-trained coaches" to justify their actions.

It does not have the right to judge the parents of children with disabilities and use discriminatory remarks.

Having the coaching certificates does not mean they are running the club correctly, fairly, or safely.

​I have escalated this to the national level as a major safeguarding risk.

We visited for Sunday lunch today after finding this place online. We were pleasantly surprised to get a table for 3 adults and a child under 2 without a booking, and first impressions were great — the pub itself is absolutely stunning inside.

Unfortunately, everything went downhill from there.

We ordered a starter and three mains, along with drinks. The drinks took ages to arrive, and in total we waited nearly an hour for the food. Normally I don’t mind a wait if the food is worth it, but what happened during that time was very strange.

One staff member came through the pub carrying two large Tesco bags. My wife noticed what looked like boxes inside, including what she thought were boxes of lamb shanks. Out of curiosity, while waiting in the car afterwards she checked Tesco online and found the exact lamb shank product — complete with a 40-minute cooking time, which matched almost perfectly with how long we waited.

I ordered the lamb shank myself and it was very chewy and definitely didn’t taste fresh, so the penny really dropped at that point.

To make matters worse, two meals were brought out first but not our 2-year-old son’s meal. He understandably started crying because everyone else had food except him. The staff disappeared for another five minutes until I asked where the final meal was. I was waved off, and eventually it arrived. Throughout the visit, staff seemed completely disorganised, with multiple members walking in and out of the kitchen empty-handed and seemingly unsure what was going on.

Such a shame because the venue itself is beautiful, but the service and food quality were hugely disappointing.

And please don’t respond saying the lamb wasn’t from Tesco — we literally bought one on the way home to compare, and it looked identical.

Avoid.

When I was given the keys, the property was not cleaned and was not in a hygienic or safe condition to move into. I made it clear from the beginning that I was pregnant, asthmatic, and later experiencing pregnancy-related mobility complications, so moving into an unsafe and unhygienic property posed serious health concerns asides my developing mobility diagnosis restricting me from using stairs. I promptly informed the agency that I wished to discontinue the tenancy due to the condition of the property and provided medical evidence from my GP.

While I was told the tenancy could be terminated once another tenant was found, I have continued to face the financial burden of paying rent and bills for this property for months while also having to secure alternative accommodation immediately for my wellbeing. This has caused enormous financial and emotional strain.
What has been especially frustrating is the apparent lack of urgency in re-letting the property, despite how quickly it was originally let to me. At one stage, I also noticed confusing marketing around the property’s availability online, which only added to my concerns.
Overall, this experience has felt deeply unfair, exhausting, and lacking in compassion or customer care. I would strongly encourage prospective tenants to thoroughly inspect any property and ensure all concerns are clearly documented before committing, especially if you're like me or my demographic. When La Cucina first opened it was absolutely class, but estimations went down hill fairly quickly.

When we first found out La Cucina had opened, me and a couple of the lads decided to give it a try and we weren't disappointed, we got in without a wait and food was amazing, in fact we ended up recommending it to everyone in our factory just across the road, we all ended up going in for for their dinner specials. For the first 3 or 4 months it became our daily place to pop in around lunchtime for some scran, we often even went in on the mornings and ordered sausage sandwiches for the whole team. Never had trouble with waiting and the food was well priced and tasted amazing. It was a lot more than the other local gaffs but was much better quality so we didn't mind.

After a little while they started to trend and got really popular on social media which meant people were travelling from all over to get in, it was a nightmare for us locals to get in for our daily scran without a 25-30 minute wait minimum, the queue was normally out the door and down the lane. People would be fighting to get through the front door.

After a while and getting sick of waiting we did start ordering in advanced so we could go pick it up on our dinner hour but over time even that started to be awful, when calling up you could never get through (we used to start around 10:15), but even when we managed to get through and pre-order we would get there and the order would be forgotten about or we would still sit around waiting 20 minutes for them to sort it out.

Overall: The food was amazing but the horrible service and waiting around on top of the prices of a special going up a couple of quid left a sour taste in our mouth, so in the end we all sacked it off and went back to our usual spot, the food might not be as good but at least it's quick and we don't have to end up binning it because it took so long to get it our lunch hour is already over.

I attended this site as an agency HGV driver collecting a trailer. While waiting, I took my legally required driving break using the driver welfare facilities (canteen area).

During this time, I was instructed to leave the site immediately and told I could be banned if I did not comply, even though I was actively taking my break and eating.

As a driver, I fully understand that sites have operational and security rules. However, there is no clear information provided to visiting drivers about:

* where legal driving breaks are allowed to be taken on site
* how UK driving break requirements are meant to be handled in practice
* whether driver welfare areas can be used during statutory breaks

Under UK driving regulations, HGV drivers are required to take mandatory breaks. In practice, drivers rely on facilities like canteens to eat and rest safely. Being interrupted while eating and threatened with removal felt unnecessary and poorly communicated.

The main issue here is not the rule itself, but the lack of clear guidance and consistency. If drivers are expected not to take breaks in welfare areas, this should be clearly stated before arrival.

Better communication would help avoid situations where drivers are trying to comply with legal driving requirements but are instead met with conflicting instructions.

I ordered a car in December, was told early February delivery, it’s now mid April and still do not have a date. They keep changing estimated dates, not processing things, causing huge delays.

Car was in the UK since at least 19/3/26

Small chip in door handle that was a 10 minute job, that they was aware of on above date still not delivered as of 13/4/26, it has spent at least 12 days in the shop.

I would strongly caution any NHS employee against entering into a salary sacrifice lease through NHS Fleet Solutions.

My experience has been defined by misinformation, inconsistency, and a complete lack of accountability. I was explicitly told by a member of staff that no early termination fee would apply if I was within the final 60 days of my lease. I acted on that advice. Despite this, I have still been charged an exit fee — with no acknowledgement of the incorrect information provided, and no effort whatsoever to resolve the situation fairly.

It is impossible to make informed decisions when the organisation’s own staff provide guidance that is later disregarded. The burden — both financial and administrative — is simply pushed back onto the customer.

What makes this worse is the selective rigidity of their policies. When it suited them, I was forced to retain a previous lease vehicle for 5 years instead of the agreed 3, with zero flexibility or consideration. Yet when I rely on their own stated terms, there is suddenly no discretion, no consistency, and no accountability.

This is not a minor administrative issue — it is a fundamental failure in governance, communication, and customer treatment.

Salary sacrifice schemes are marketed as straightforward and supportive for NHS staff. In reality, this experience has been anything but. The lack of transparency and the willingness to financially penalise customers based on their own internal miscommunication is deeply concerning.

My advice? Avoid entirely. If you do proceed, assume that verbal assurances are meaningless, ensure everything is documented in writing, and be prepared for terms to be enforced in a way that does not reflect what you have been told.

This provider has one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve dealt with.

From day one after moving into our new-build property, we experienced issues accessing mobile apps—particularly banking apps. A ticket was raised, and while there were attempts to troubleshoot, most of the responses were the usual scripted advice like “reboot the router,” which clearly wasn’t addressing the root cause.

After ongoing issues, it became apparent that the problem stems from how the service is configured for new homeowners—specifically, the lack of a static public IP unless you pay extra. Once a static IP was assigned, the issue was resolved immediately.

Instead of acknowledging this as a known limitation or configuration issue, customer support repeatedly shifted the blame onto our devices, claiming they were incompatible. This is despite multiple devices being affected, which should have made it obvious the problem was network-related.

Rather than offering a transparent explanation, the only solutions presented were to either pay for a static IP or continue rebooting the router—neither of which was acceptable given the circumstances.

Special mention to Ewan and the team: the support provided was consistently unhelpful and dismissive. Overall, a very frustrating experience.

If I could leave less than 1 star I would. I bought this tour as a xmas gift for my parents, one is a physically disabled wheelchair user, and the other has dementia and needs a wheelchair for long distances. Our tour consisted of another wheelchair user and several people using walking sticks and walking aids. Tour guide Mel consistently started her talks at each location with no consideration for the impaired members of the group. This meant by the time they caught up they had missed half the content and they couldnt hear or see the remainder of it due to everyone stood in front of them. Im aware that its a live set and often gravelled paths, however my parent wheelchair got stuck on 3 occasions in the gravel. Mel ignored us physically dragging the 15 stone chair across the gravel ourselves to free it, not once were we asked if we were ok. We were not the only impaired people on the tour who felt ignored as, as we were often lagging behind the wheelchair users were often left together. The last time my parent’s wheelchair got stuck they were that embarrassed, upset and humiliated they sat there and cried and begged to go home. A second staff member did come over to offer support, they were more understanding and considerate. When we arrived the security staff told us to head to disabled parking and that they would radio down to make someone aware we were on our way. No one approached us and we didnt know where to go. I had to ask 3 staff members before someone pointed us in the right direction. None of the doors to toilets or in and put the building are manageable for a disabled person to navigate without help.
Giving the fact a lot of emmerdales audience are of the older generation, the lack of care and consideration is disgraceful. There is literally a coach pulling in to collect and drop off constantly. There should be a dedicated disabled tour option once a day or several times a week where staff should have more awareness that they may need to talk quieter, and be more patient and supportive. The attitude of Mel was absolutely disgusting. It takes a lot to persuade my parents to brave actually doing anything due to their difficulties and this negative experience will be a massive set back for individuals who are already isolated. They paid the same amount of money as everyone else to be there, although my sister and myself were there as carers, we do not watch the show and were specifically there to support my parents ability to enjoy a day out together. Clearly a massive focus on money making with little consideration to their fans/ audience and paying customers. Avoid this tour if you have additional needs or are a wheelchair user.

Initial communication became difficult when the sales representative, Matt, requested to change my planned collection day from Saturday to another day without clear explanation. When I referenced their advertised 7-day opening, his tone became rude and aggressive, pressuring me for an exact time despite my reasonable schedule constraints.

Upon visiting the dealership on April 25th as agreed, my partner and I inspected the vehicle and found multiple issues: dents and scratches on various panels, paint damage, interior wear, and only one key available despite no prior disclosure. The manager pointed out damage and scuffs on my trade-in vehicle, suggesting a £400 deduction for repainting, which I feel was excessive and inconsistent given the condition of the Range Rover on offer.

It has taken me a long time to write this due to how traumatic the experience was, but I feel it’s important to share so that others are aware before booking.
I visited Bumpkins York in October 2024 when I was around 10–11 weeks pregnant. This was my first pregnancy, and I was excited to finally have a scan. On arrival, the staff were pleasant enough. However, the experience quickly became distressing once I was taken into the scan room.
The sonographer began the scan and soon said that what she was seeing was not what she would expect at that stage of pregnancy. As this was my first pregnancy, I didn’t fully understand what was happening. I was then left in the room with my partner, looking at a large image of what appeared to be an empty uterus on a big screen, while the sonographer left for quite some time with very little explanation.
When she returned, she told me she had contacted the maternity department at Scarborough Hospital and advised me to go to A&E with a suspected miscarriage. I left the room extremely upset. Unfortunately, due to the layout of the clinic, I had to walk past another couple waiting happily for their appointment while I was visibly distressed. There is no privacy for patients receiving bad news, which made an already awful situation even worse.
I then travelled to Scarborough Hospital, only to be told that a scan could not be performed because it was a Saturday. This meant I had to wait 48 hours in a highly distressed state before being seen by the early pregnancy unit.
Throughout this experience, I felt there was very little compassion or professionalism shown by Bumpkins. I received no follow-up support afterward—only a request to leave a review, which I did at the time and received no response to.
I want other women to be aware of the potential risks of visiting private clinics for pregnancy scans, particularly in situations like this. There seemed to be no clear protocol for handling such sensitive circumstances. In my opinion, scans should not be carried out on weekends if appropriate follow-up care cannot be arranged promptly. Additionally, there is currently no legal requirement in the UK for those performing these scans to hold specific qualifications or professional registration, which raises serious concerns about patient safety.

Six years ago, Northern Gas & Power were excellent. Andy Bell acted as our utility broker and negotiated a very good deal for our business. While there were some setup issues at the time - including direct debits not being set up correctly and our company being billed for another business’s utilities - overall the service was still worthwhile.

Unfortunately, over the years the level of service has declined dramatically. During the second contract arranged by Andy, there were serious errors in how the account was set up. As a result, our company was incorrectly billed for the energy usage of two other businesses, totalling over £30k. We repeatedly tried to contact Andy to resolve this, but after weeks of getting nowhere we were eventually told to deal directly with the suppliers instead.

In hindsight, we should not have entered into a third contract arranged by Andy. He is very persuasive and attentive during the contract-signing stage, but once the agreement is in place he becomes extremely difficult (if not impossible) to contact.

Andy convinced us to enter into new gas and electricity contracts for our portfolio of 23 properties, due to start on 1 October. After signing the contracts, we received no further information. We were not even told who the supplier was until direct debits began leaving our bank account.

When I asked Andy why we had not received any bills, he sent a generic link to E.ON’s online billing system and told me to set up an account. However, creating an online account requires account numbers, which we were never provided. I sent multiple follow-up emails, and, after more than four weeks of chasing, I have still received no response.

I eventually had to contact E.ON directly and provide every single property address to establish whether they supplied our sites. Of the 23 properties, E.ON confirmed that they only supply one site for electricity only. Despite this, 11 direct debits labelled “E.ON first payment” have been taken from our business account.

As E.ON only supplies one of our properties, it appears we are once again paying for electricity that does not belong to us. E.ON cannot tell us whose accounts these payments relate to, as we have no authority on them.They advised us to contact the broker directly. When I explained who the broker was, the E.ON representative laughed and said she had been trying to contact Northern Gas & Power for months without success.

In addition, we are now almost three months into the new contracts allegedly being set up, and I still have no idea who currently supplies our properties with gas.

Overall, our experience has been extremely frustrating, costly, and time-consuming. What was once a good service has become unreliable and unresponsive, and we would not recommend Northern Gas & Power based on our recent experiences.

Absolutely shocking experience.
I ordered a steak with mash, veg (turnip, carrots, cabbage) and onion rings for £25, expecting at least a decent standard. I asked for the steak medium rare, and it came out well done — and I don’t mean “slightly over,” I mean cremated. If I wanted it that cooked, I’d have brought a chisel instead of a knife. It was completely overdone, dry, and honestly like chewing on leather… just with less flavour. It had zero taste — I’ve had more flavour from chewing gum after an hour.
The only reason I forced it down was because I wanted the protein and didn’t want the money to be a total waste — otherwise I would have sent it straight back.
The quality was embarrassingly poor. I can genuinely make a far better steak at home from the supermarket for about £7, and it tastes miles better than what I was served here — and mine doesn’t come with a side of regret.
The onion rings were just as bad — soft, soggy, and not crispy at all, like they’d been microwaved or reheated. More like onion “sadness” than onion rings.
The vegetables had a strange smell, and after everything else, I couldn’t even bring myself to eat them. At that point I wasn’t sure if it was veg or a science experiment.
Hygiene was also a big issue. The glasses were dirty, the carpets inside were thick with dust, and under my table there was clearly leftover food from a previous customer — some kind of mashed potato that I didn’t notice at first and ended up getting on my shoe. Nothing like taking part of someone else’s meal home with you.
Overall, a terrible experience from start to finish. I genuinely don’t understand how this place has 5-star reviews — unless they’re coming from people who think charcoal is a seasoning.
AVOID.

I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction following a recent school trip to your vegan farm, which I attended as a parent helper. While I fully respect that veganism is an important and valid lifestyle choice, I was extremely uncomfortable with the way it was presented to the children during our visit.

At the conclusion of the trip, the host delivered what I can only describe as a highly inappropriate and one-sided talk. The children were told that they should only eat plant-based foods and that consuming farm animals is morally wrong, even being compared to eating their own cousins. I found this language entirely unsuitable for a group of young children. It was not framed as an introduction to veganism or a balanced discussion, but rather as a set of absolute beliefs presented as fact. This approach felt more like an attempt to impose a viewpoint than to educate.

I have no issue whatsoever with children learning about veganism, and I would welcome my own child being informed about different dietary choices in a balanced and age-appropriate way. However, making children feel guilty or morally wrong for eating foods they have grown up with is not acceptable. It is particularly concerning that such strong and emotive opinions were delivered without parental consent or any opportunity for discussion.

In addition to this, the overall structure of the visit was disappointing. There was no clear educational content relating to farming practices, and we did not see any fruit, vegetables, or crops, which was unexpected given the nature of the farm. The children were left to play unstructured games outdoors in cold weather, with little organisation or meaningful engagement.
Overall, the experience was poorly managed and left me feeling extremely uncomfortable.

I would not recommend this venue to other schools seeking an educational and inclusive trip.

one_star_reviews.text:
Continuous calls received by your sales team, after repeatedly asking to cancel my number from your database.

Complete disregard of the fact I clearly expressed several times I am not interested and I do not to wish to spend my time discussing your product/service.

It has been a disappointing experience.

I first engaged with BigChange in January 2025. By no fault of Big Change themselves, we weren't able to complete the onboarding process and use the software for the 13 months we were subscribed (costing thousands). We are a small company, and didn't have the time or resources to complete training and integrate it within our workflow.

My poor review isn't relating to the product, but rather, their ethics. The first major dissapointment relates to their cooersive selling techniques used to sell it to us. My second dissapointment relates to their immoral technique of charging one month more, despite giving realistically, plenty of notice for us to cancel. It made the cancelling process very stressful and expensive, and does a great deal of harm for a small business, for which they don't care about at all.

I think the platform looks great, but just be very wary before you register, and make your own judgement call on whether you have time to set it up, rather than rely on the sales team to convince you otherwise. I will not be recommending their company to others in the service industry.

04/05/2026 Edit: This review keeps being removed, as have other one star reviews since I wrote this back in Oct 2025. Customers be aware.

We had extremely high hopes for BigChange, but our experience has been deeply disappointing from start to finish.

The sales process was far more pressurised than we expected from a professional software provider. Calls regularly ran late into the evening and there was a strong sense of urgency to get us to sign the agreement. On one occasion we remained on a sales call until very late while being pushed to move forward with the contract. The overall tone felt less like a consultative sales process and more like a high-pressure attempt to secure a deal.

Unfortunately, once onboarding began and we started actually using the system, it quickly became clear that the platform did not align with the operational workflow that had been discussed during the sales process.

Our business operates technicians nationally, with constantly changing start and finish locations. During sales discussions we were assured that BigChange would support this type of operation through flexible scheduling and route optimisation. In reality, the system appears heavily designed around technicians starting and finishing at a fixed base location. While BigChange claim this can be configured, the practical reality is that it requires significant manual intervention and undermines the efficiency the software is supposed to deliver.

Another major issue is the reliance on geofencing or What3Words to properly identify jobs at the same site. In our industry we frequently complete multiple jobs within the same cemetery or site address. Not every job record will have a geofence or precise coordinate attached, something we clearly explained during the sales process. Despite this, the system still struggles to clearly surface jobs at the same location unless those additional layers are configured, meaning our preferred workflow simply does not function properly.

The route optimiser itself was also a major disappointment. What was demonstrated during the sales process appeared quick and intuitive. In reality it involves far more steps than expected and feels slow and cumbersome compared with other systems we have used. For teams planning routes daily, this creates unnecessary friction rather than saving time.

The onboarding process also caused significant issues. We had been very clear about our timeframe because we needed to give notice to our existing software provider. However, delays during onboarding meant that by the time we were able to properly access and configure the platform we had only around three weeks to realistically test and implement it within our operations. That is simply not enough time to properly deploy a system of this scale.

There are also several usability decisions that make day-to-day operations unnecessarily difficult. For example, the “cancel” button deletes jobs entirely rather than simply removing them from the schedule, which is counterintuitive and introduces risk when managing large volumes of work.

Perhaps most disappointing was the response when we raised our concerns. When we informed our account manager, Ryan, that we intended to cancel due to these operational issues, the immediate response was that we would be expected to pay the full contract value. There was little attempt to understand the problems we had encountered or to discuss them constructively. The conversation felt focused solely on enforcing the contract rather than addressing the legitimate concerns we had raised.

Overall, the platform feels heavily designed for a very specific type of field service business and far less flexible than it is presented during the sales process. For companies operating nationally or requiring dynamic scheduling workflows, it may prove extremely difficult to adapt the system to your real operational needs.

Based on our experience, any business considering BigChange should insist on a genuine hands-on trial and test their real scheduling workflow thoroughly before committing to a contract.

I would not recommend renting a property through this landlord. My experience has been extremely disappointing.

I have been raising concerns about severe mould in my rented property since 2019. At the time, a tradesman they sent out told me the issue was caused by me drying clothes on the radiators. I followed this advice and bought a tumble dryer, but the mould problem continued.

In 2024, after reporting the issue again, I was once more told that the mould was due to poor ventilation caused by my own habits and was advised to buy a dehumidifier. I did this, yet the problem still remained unresolved.

It took seven years of repeated complaints before someone finally came out and properly inspected the property, confirming that the house is indeed riddled with mould.

This situation is especially concerning as I now have a newborn baby sleeping in a room next to a loft that is badly affected by mould. My child already had a difficult start in life and spent time in ICU due to breathing difficulties when born, so living in these conditions is extremely worrying.

After years of being dismissed and told the problem was my fault, someone finally listened to my concerns and carried out a proper inspection.

Overall, the way this issue has been handled has been unacceptable.

Our experience with River Vets was nothing short of a nightmare, and I feel it’s my responsibility to warn other pet owners.

We trusted Alex at River Vets to carry out routine castration on our young rescue dog, Kimbo. He convinced us to allow three procedures at once (castration, dental cleaning, and treatment for “happy tail”) since the dog would already be under anaesthetic. That decision was a disaster.
•	Castration: Left Kimbo with a huge haematoma, severe bruising, two infections, and an agonising 8-week recovery (see photo). This is not what competent surgery looks like.
•	Dental cleaning: Performed at the same time as castration – something we later found out should never be done, since bacteria from the teeth can spread and cause infection. This reckless decision almost certainly explains the infections that followed.
•	Happy tail treatment: Supposedly a “straightforward” cauterisation, but it was so badly executed that Kimbo ultimately lost his entire tail (see photo).

This is a dog who had already survived unimaginable abuse before coming to us – beaten, starved, and burned with cigarettes. Instead of receiving the compassionate and professional care he deserved, he was left mutilated and traumatised yet again by negligent veterinary care.

For comparison, our second dog (same age, same breed, same operation) was neutered at Alnorthumbria a few months later and walked out absolutely fine, with zero recovery time. That tells you everything you need to know about the difference in standards.

Avoid — £2,000 wasted on a service that delivered nothing.

We engaged Flat Fee Recruiter for three basic roles and spent close to £2,000. Across all three, not a single candidate they put forward was suitable for so much as a first-stage interview.

The core of their pitch is screening — vetting and shortlisting candidates so you don't have to wade through irrelevant CVs. In our experience, no meaningful screening was done. What we received was a high-volume dump of unscreened, low-quality CVs that we still had to sift through ourselves. Even after we chased them for a shortlist, the single candidate they produced couldn't start for months — despite the role being advertised, and confirmed in writing, as immediate-start. That alone tells you how much attention they paid to the brief.

The pattern was depressingly familiar: attentive and engaged up to the point the invoice was paid, then radio silence. Once they had our money, the service effectively disappeared.

You will get better results, spend less money, and waste less of your own time by posting directly on LinkedIn and Indeed using their free tiers. Flat Fee Recruiter added zero value to our hiring process and behaved like cowboys. I'd strongly urge any business considering them to look elsewhere.

NEGLIGENT, DISHONEST AND UNPROFESSIONAL BEYOND BELIEF – DO NOT RISK IT

We booked a home birth with Amie through Private Midwives and the ‘care’ I received from her was so awful in so many ways that I don’t know where to begin. My baby was born by emergency caesarean due to an undiagnosed breech which was not discovered until the 2nd stage of labour.

Amie failed to suspect the breech during 3 antenatal appointments, where she recorded the baby as head down. I should have been sent for a scan to check the presentation, but I wasn’t. But what is much worse, and what we only learnt later, is that Amie and her colleague should have been performing abdominal palpations during my labour to check the position of the baby. They did not do this even once. So not only did these midwives miss that the baby was breech – they were not even looking! Instead, they falsified these readings in the notes.

AMIE ALSO DISAPPEARED FROM MY HOMEBIRTH FOR 3 HOURS, just 1 hour after she had arrived. Not a word was said by either midwife about where she had gone or why. We later found out that AMIE HAD TAKEN HERSELF UPSTAIRS AND SLEPT IN OUR BED, WITHOUT OUR PERMISSION.

Amie and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF LABOUR. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway at 10:30 in the morning. They have since lied and said I gave them permission to do this. I did not.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. It was recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and me and my husband were told to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with Amie. Despite this, neither Amie or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Amie or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Amie and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone. They could not have come upstairs without our knowing it.

Despite neither Amie or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Amie and her colleague also tried to blame this on me and my husband, by saying that we told her not to ring one – another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was also not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). Amie and her colleague listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. During this time, they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings. These are just some of the issues with the ‘care’ I received and some of the lies Amie has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Amie to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

Here is a polished, clear version of your review, ready to post:
AVOID THIS GARAGE. DO NOT BUY A VEHICLE FROM HERE.

To be honest, you would think the people running this place have never run a business before. I bought a van from them; it looked great on the outside, and the staff were very friendly—right up until the moment I signed the papers. As soon as you go back to report a problem, the attitude changes completely and they just give you excuses.

The list of issues:

1. Side lights: Reported they weren't working before I bought it. They said they would fix them, but they never did.

2. Roof: The roof on the Luton van was loose. I ended up fixing that myself.

3. Timing Belt: About 4 weeks later, the van broke down. They claimed the timing belt had been changed, and it was still under the 3-month warranty. Despite this, they still charged me £2,500 to fix it.

4. Mechanical Failures: The starter motor broke. They did the front brakes but said the back ones needed replacing. That’s when they also told me the rear shock absorbers needed changing too.

5. Engine Recall: I took it to a Citroën dealership because of a safety recall. They did a report and found the engine needs replacing. The quote? £14,000.

And it doesn't stop there...
They told me the van came with 3 months road tax and that they would send off for the logbook. I drove it for 3 months while they kept saying "it takes time". When I checked with the DVLA, there was no tax and no logbook registered. I was driving illegally!

When I confronted them, it was a nightmare. They tried to tell me to go to the post office and sort it myself. I refused, so eventually, they sorted the logbook—but then had the cheek to tell me I had to pay half the road tax myself!

Summary: Very friendly sales patter, but shocking service and vehicles that are clearly not roadworthy or correctly registered once you hand over the cash.

Purchased an Evoque in May 2025. Didn’t haggle. Perfect customer. Gave them too much trust and was taken advantage of. Lesson learnt. Terrible aftercare and a really poor overall experience. The rear diff was not working so the back wheels were just grinding (how did that get through an MOT 🤦‍♂️). Absolutely shocking to even let me drive it away!

I was told the brakes had been done, yet within weeks of actually getting the car the brake pad warning light came on. Again, this and the rear diff raises serious questions about how genuine the advisory free MOT and pre delivery checks actually were. No legitimate garage would have signed that car off in the condition it arrived in especially with no advisory’s as again, three months later the front brakes went to steel. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others to avoid this dealership.

one_star_reviews.text:
I have visited the South Tynedale Railway many times over the years, and it’s a railway I feel has a lot of potential, which is why some recent developments have been disappointing.

While the extension to Slaggyford runs through attractive countryside, the reality is that there is very little to do at the current terminus. Aside from the buffet coach at the station there are no shops, pubs, or cafés in the village, which can make the wait for the return train unnecessarily long if you are not planning to go walking.

As an enthusiast, I was also extremely disappointed by the recent work carried out on historic steam locomotive "Barber". In my opinion the locomotive’s distinctive historic appearance has been unnecessarily altered, creating a rather odd and unattractive looking engine. It also appears that original material may have been altered or lost in the process. The reasoning given for these changes has been widely questioned, and the work could instead have been carried out in a way that preserved more of the locomotive’s original character, for example by following the appearance of its sister engine "Masham". The way this was handled has been very controversial and has clearly divided opinion within the enthusiast community.

It is also disappointing to see the railway using AI-generated images in its advertising. For a heritage railway, it would be far more appropriate to use genuine photography of the line or support real artists.

Overall, this railway still has potential given its scenic location, but recent decisions have made it difficult to feel enthusiastic about visiting again.
